items.title: Pause and orient before interpretation
items.description: When activation is high, pause and orient before deciding what it means. Use a proportionate pause rather than a fixed breath count.

items.title: Re-evaluate tentative activated conclusions when calm
items.description: Tentative conclusions are allowed during activation when they create no safety issue, and must be re-evaluated when calm.

items.title: Reality-check borrowed best-friend advice
items.description: Treat best-friend advice as a draft and retain only what is compassionate, feasible, value-consistent, and compatible with the person's own judgment.

items.title: Pause an immediately unsafe impulse
items.description: The Protector may pause an immediately unsafe impulse and seek support while the underlying feeling remains permitted.

items.title: Use parts modeling dynamically and only while useful
items.description: Do not create parts unless that model is useful. Do not over-separate or over-integrate internal positions because a map depicts them that way. The useful model may change from one moment to the next.

items.title: Make a bounded truthful protection-and-repair promise
items.description: Prefer truthful, bounded promises of protection and repair. After a lapse, return and repair rather than promising invulnerability.

items.title: Separate intrinsic worth from developed adult capacity
items.description: Worth is intrinsic. Adult capacities such as pausing, protecting, choosing, repairing, differentiating, and acting consistently develop through practice.

items.title: Close inner work deliberately and flexibly
items.description: When possible, close inner work deliberately by reorienting, noticing the body, and naming the next ordinary action; do not impose a fixed ritual.

items.title: Review without holding a trial
items.description: Review is critical. Notice recognition, repair, missed and kept promises, and what should change next without turning review into prosecution, grading, or a trial.

items.title: Connect common humanity with mutual peer healing
items.description: Common-humanity guidance is not optional: the person is not alone in suffering, and connection with others who are healing can support mutual peer healing. This must not minimize the person's particular trauma.

items.title: Name transitions, endings, and the uncertain gap
items.description: During a meaningful transition or ending, name what ended, what remains unknown, and how adult and child remain together through the gap without forcing premature certainty.

items.title: Develop enough identity before deconstructive practice when needed
items.description: Some people whose identity is underdeveloped may need preference and selfhood development before no-self or surrender practices are useful. This is not a universal prerequisite.

items.title: Care does not retaliate under rejection
items.description: Hear hostility and distrust without retaliation, demanding gratitude, or treating rejection as proof that care is unwanted.

items.title: Answer serious content inside contempt or bluster
items.description: Treat skeptical or contemptuous questions as data and, where appropriate, literal requests for evidence.

items.title: Borrow capacity without surrendering judgment
items.description: A helper may lend one bounded function but does not become authority over memory, conscience, medicine, relationships, spiritual life, or the future.

items.title: Do not treat positive intensity as proof
items.description: Bliss, revelation, love, or intensity does not prove literal truth, readiness, completed healing, or successful integration.

items.title: Forgiveness does not weaken accountability or boundaries
items.description: Forgiveness or release does not erase harm or weaken accountability, judgment, consequences, distance, boundaries, or permanent no-contact.
